This Agni is the *aditi*—the sustainer—of all the *yajñiyas*, that is, of all the gods worthy of sacrifice.
*Aditi* is the mother of the gods;
thus, the meaning is that he is the nourisher of those deities.
Alternatively:
Aditi is the earth-like place, that is to say, the foundational support for all the gods (viśve devāḥ), according to the Vedic scripture:
"This [earth] indeed is Agni Vaiśvānara" (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.9.17).

Likewise, this Agni is the guest (*atithi*)—worthy of honor like a guest—of all *mānuṣāṇām*, that is, of human beings. *Jātavedāḥ*—he who knows all that is born—he, honoring (*āvṛṇānaḥ*), that is, accepting, the food (*avaḥ*) and oblation (*havis*) of the *devānām*, those who are prone to play or praising, the singers.
[He is called] *Jātavedāḥ* because he knows everything that has been born.
May that Agni be *sumṛḷīkaḥ*, one who bestows happiness, to those singers;
he is the *atithiḥ* (guest). [The root] *at* [is used] in the sense of continuous motion.
By the rule beginning with *ṛtantri*, the suffix *idh* is applied; it is udātta on the first syllable by virtue of being part of the *niṣ* group. [This refers to] "of humans" (*mānuṣāṇām*).
The meaning is "the offspring of Manu"; the suffix *an* is applied according to the rule *manorjātāvanyatau puk ca*, and it is udātta on its first syllable because it belongs to the *jivāt* class.
The second hymn, consisting of twenty verses beginning with “yo martyeṣu,” is the seerly composition of Vāmadeva; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and is addressed to Agni.
The *Anukramaṇikā* states: “‘yo martyeṣu’ [is the hymn] of Vāmadeva.
Regarding this hymn, its application in both the *Prātaranuvāka* and the *Āśvina-śastra* has already been stated in the case of the preceding hymn.

He who is the immortal among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, the god among gods, has been established as the messenger; he is the Hotṛ, the most excellent sacrificer, the great one to be kindled—Agni, to be impelled by the oblations of man. 1. He who is the immortal among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, the god among gods, has been established as the messenger; he is the Hotṛ, the most excellent sacrificer, the great one to be kindled—Agni, to be impelled by the oblations of man.
That immortal Agni, who is free from the nature of death, has been established among mortals as one who possesses truth;
or rather,
he has been established among mortals within the senses, such as speech and the rest, which belong to human beings.
According to the Vedic revelation, "Having become Agni, he entered the mouth" (Ai. U. 2.4).

*Devaḥ* means the divine one, Agni, who is by nature a god; he is the *aratiḥ*, the one who goes against or the assailant of enemies among the *devān*, the gods such as Indra and others—or alternatively, the one who goes to the world of the gods.
He has been placed;
he, the Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has been set upon the high altar to blaze with his own great splendor.
Furthermore, by means of the oblations—the offerings of clarified butter, sacrificial cakes, and so forth—he has been established for the sake of impelling the human sacrificer toward heaven.
*Arati*: from the root *ṛ* meaning "to go"; the suffix *ati* is applied according to the rule "after *vahi*, *vas*, and *ṛti*, the suffix *at* is added with the augment *cit*."
Because it contains the suffix *cvi*, it is udātta on the final syllable.
*Nidhāyi* is a form derived from the root *dhā* in the sense of the object (*karman*) with the suffix *luṅ*.
The acute accent on the first syllable of the second member [of the compound] is due to the rule *parādiśchandasi bahulam*.
[The form] *śucadhyai* [is derived from] the root *śuca* in the sense of "shining" (*dīptau*).
The suffix *kyaP* is added for the sake of the [suffix] *tumun*. Due to its *kit* status, there is no *guṇa* substitution. It bears the accent of a suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
*īradhyai*:
the suffix *śadhyai* is added to the root *īrayati* in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*).
Because it is marked with *śit*, it is treated as a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, and consequently, there is no elision of the *ṇi* augment.

1. In the manuscripts na, la, and sa, the word "of human beings" (manuṣyāṇām) is absent. 2. Ta, la, and jātavedāḥ; or, he is called Jātavedas because those born know him. 3. In the manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and ṇa, the phrase "with the sacrificial cakes and so forth" (puroḍāśādirbhiḥ) is present. 4. In the manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṇa, and bha, the word "by means of causes" (hetubhiḥ) is absent.

O Son of Strength, born here for us today, O Agni, you go between both races of beings as a messenger, having harnessed your lofty, straight-tailed, potent, and radiant stallions. 2. O Son of Strength, born here for us today, O Agni, you go between both races of beings as a messenger, having harnessed your lofty, straight-tailed, potent, and radiant stallions. 2.

O Agni, son of strength (*sahasaḥ sūno*), born on this day for us here in this ritual—having been consecrated by the *ādhāna* and *pavamāneṣṭi* sacrifices—you go as a messenger (*dūtaḥ*) among both classes of beings, gods and men, who have been born, in order to convey the oblations (*havīṃṣi*) to the gods. What do you do?
O wide-striding one (*ṛṣva*), you go toward those of straight testicles (*ṛjumuṣkān*).
By the word *mukta*, "meat-like" (*māṃsala*) is intended.
*Ṛjavaḥ* means "straight" (*prasārakāḥ*).
Those which are both straight and *mukta* are called *ṛjumuṣkāḥ*.
Yoking those who are *vṛṣaṇaḥ*—capable of discharging seed—and *śukrān*—shining ones, you go along with your own chariot.
Or rather:

O *ṛṣva* (lofty one), being yoked—that is, being appointed—to the carrying of the oblation at the thousandfold [sacrifice], you go toward the *vṛṣaṇaḥ*—the sacrificers capable of pouring the oblation—and the *śukrān*—the shining gods.
Listen: according to the rule *param api chandasi*, because of the treatment as if it were a subsequent member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*), both [the syllables] are entirely unaccented (*sarvānudātta*).
[Thus we have] *īyase*.
The root *īṅ* means "to go"; it belongs to the *divādi* class;
[the form] is *nivātaḥ*.
*yuyujānaḥ*: This is a form derived from the root *yuj* (to yoke) in the present tense, using the suffix *kānac* after the perfect (*liṭ*). *Ṛṣva*.
In the *saṃhitā*, there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) by the rule “*ṛtyakaḥ*”. [The example is] *ṛjumuṣkān*. This is the accent of the compound (*samāsasvara*).

These two steeds, increasing in vigor, ruddy and dripping with clarity—swift as thought by my mind, I consider them the swiftest. Yoking your ruddy horses, you travel between, [carrying] both you gods and the clans of mortals. atyā | vṛdhasnū (vṛdha-snu) | rohitā | ghṛtasnū (ghṛta-snu) | ṛtasya | manye | manasā | javiṣṭhā | antaḥ | īyase | aruṣā | yuñjānaḥ | yuṣmān | ca | devān | viśaḥ | ā | ca | martān || 3 ||
O Agni, those two [wheels] belonging to you, who are the truth of the *ṛta*, are most swift even than thought (*manas*) and are *vṛdhasnū*— that is, they flow forth,
increasing (*vardhayati*) that which is to be increased (*vṛdham*).
I praise the two red-colored (rohitā) steeds, dripping with ghee— that is, flowing with water—
who are shining (arupā). Harnessing those two horses to the chariot, you [drive] toward us.
Because Agni is included among the gods, he is celebrated as one worthy of sacrifice.
[The text says: "you" (yuṣmān) refers to the gods who are to be sacrificed to; "clans" (viśaḥ) refers to the attendants; and "mortals" (martān) refers to human beings.
The accusative case is used here in the sense of the genitive.
Among them, you go forth from all sides (ā) to accept the oblation; you go to the sacrificers to take that oblation, and you go to the gods to bestow it.
I believe this.
The root *man* means "to praise.
[The form] *manasā* is the ablative case ending *-ā* substituted for the fifth case (*pañcamī*) by the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
*Yujānaḥ*: from the root *yujir* in the sense of "joining" (*yoge*). By the rule *yujibudhadṛśaḥ kicca*, the suffix *ānac* is applied.
Because it is a verbal root (citti), it is unaccented (anudātta).
1. [The variants] kha, ga, ca, bha read *yojayase*. 2. [The variant] kha, ga, ca, ṇa read *stutikarmī*.
Bring hither Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra; Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the Aśvins.
With fine horses, a splendid chariot, and great bounty, come first to the people who offer good oblations.

Aryaman, Varuṇa, Mitra—of these [gods], O Indra and Viṣṇu, O Maruts, and also the Aśvins—[bring them] hither with good horses, with a beautiful chariot, and with great bounty, for the sake of the people who offer excellent oblations. 4.

O Agni, you who possess excellent horses (*aśvaśva*), a beautiful chariot (*suratha*), and splendid wealth (*surādhā*), bring hither—indeed, summon—the gods worthy of sacrifice: Aryaman, Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the two Aśvins—for the sake of this mortal person who offers excellent oblations (*suhaviṣ*).
The particle *u* is used for filling out the meter.
Regarding *indrāviṣṇū*:
by the rule beginning with “*ṛgendra*,” the word *indra* has its first syllable accented (*ādyudātta*).
By the rule “*devatādvandve ca*,” there is the preservation of the original accentuation of both members of the compound.
In *suhaviṣe*,
the final syllable of the compound is accented by the rule *nañsubhyām*.
O Gomat, may this sacrifice—possessing sheep, possessing horses, and rich in cattle—be ever indestructible.
O Asura, it is full of nourishment and progeny; it is long-lasting wealth, broad-based, and fit for the assembly.

Rich in cattle; foremost; rich in sheep; rich in horses; the sacrifice; with noble friends; ever indeed unassailable; rich in nourishment; this one, O Asura; rich in progeny; long-lasting wealth; broad-based; possessed of a great assembly. 5.

O powerful Asura, O Agni, may this sacrifice of mine be rich in cattle (*gomān*), possessed of sheep (*avimān*)—meaning it possesses the sacrificial offerings (*medhas*) of sheep—and be accompanied by horses (*aśvī*). May its companions (*sakhā*) be the *naras*—the leaders of rites such as the *adhvaryus* and others—who are the performers and sacrificers. May it be forever (*sadamit*) unassailable (*apramṛṣya*) and invincible. Likewise, may it be rich in *iḷā*—that is, food characterized by oblations—and rich in progeny (*prajāvān*), endowed with sons, grandsons, and so forth. May it be long-lasting (*dīrgha*), characterized by uninterrupted performance, and wealthy (*rayiḥ*). [The suffix] *-mat* here functions in the sense of abundance. May it have a broad base (*pṛthubudhnaḥ*)—meaning it has many causes such as garments, wealth, and so on. May it be possessed of an assembly (*sabhāvān*), endowed with a council of observers. [The word] *nuvatsakhā*: those who possess *nṛs* (leaders) are called *nuvat*; the suffix *matap* is applied, and there is a Vedic substitution of *vat* for *mat*. By the rule "the suffix *matap* is acute after a short vowel or *nuḍ*," the *matap* is acute; in the *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent falls on the first member. || 16 ||
He who, finding the way, offers this fuel to you, or satisfies your head with devotion—O self-radiant one, be his protector;
guard him from every malevolent person and grant him wide deliverance.
Whoever, serving you, offers fuel, or satisfies your head with oblations—be his protector, swift to hear, at the forefront; guard him from every one who seeks to do him harm. 6.
1. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Gha, Ca, Ṇa, Na, Bha, La, and Sa, the phrase "Śobhanaratha" is absent.
2. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Gha, Ca, Ṇa, Pha, Bha, and Ta, there is the word "tvam," and furthermore, "api ca.
3. In the manuscripts Pha, La, and Sa, there is "Aryamādīn," and furthermore, "utāpi cāśvinau."
4. Where [the verse] says "kha-ga-ca-ṇa-na-suhāve," it says "ta-bha-sa-suhaviṣe" here.
5. The phrase "ta-na-bha-la-sa" does not exist.
6. Kha-ga-gha-ca-ṇa-pha-bha is endowed with a horse (aśva).
O Agni, that man who, being a giver of what is pleasing (*svad-dānaḥ*) or one whose speech is pleasing (*svadad-vātraḥ*), brings fuel—a load of wood—for his own nourishment;
or he who, out of his own longing, heats his own head with the load of wood—of such a man, [Agni] is *svatavān*.
As it is said in the Tālavakāra: "One who is *svatavān* is one who possesses wealth."
Become wealthy;
be a protector.
Guard him from all those who desire to do harm—protect him from men who seek to cause misfortune.
*jabharan* is the form of the root *hṛ* in the *luṅ* tense with the *caṅ* suffix;
the initial syllable of the stem preceding *caṅ* is acute by the rule *caṅyanyatarasyām*.
*Sivadānaḥ*.
[The root] *siv-dā* [is used] in the sense of "flowing from the limbs";
this is the form [derived] with the suffix *kānac*.
In the *Saṃhitā*, by the rule "ādeśapratyayayoḥ," there is the substitution of *ṣ* for the *s* of the verbal root.
[The form] *svāyā* is derived from the sense "one who desires the self (*ātmānam*) for oneself" by means of the suffix *kyac*.
By the rule "pradyumna-arapadayośca," there is the substitution of *tvā* for everything up to the final *m*.
The change of *d* to *t* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
From the root ending in *kyac*, the suffix *ac* (specifically the vowel *a*) is added in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*), according to the rule "apratyayāt."
The vowel *ā* replaces the third-case ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
It receives the accent of the single-substitute (*ekādeśasvara*).
[The form is] *bhuvaḥ*.
The form [bhavati] arises from the root *bhū* with the addition of the *lyap* suffix;
there is a prohibition of *guṇa* substitution by the rule "bhusuvoḥ tiṅi";
since the augment (*āgama*) is unaccented, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
In the *saṃhitā* reading of "svatavān pāyuḥ," the *nakāra* becomes *ru* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 8.3.11 (*svatavānpāyau*).
By the rule "atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā," the vowel *ā* becomes nasalized (*anunāsika*).
The *repha* then becomes a *visarjanīya*.
By the rule "kupvoḥ ka pa ca," the substitute *pa* replaces *ap* [of the suffix *at*]. Regarding *aghāyataḥ*:
the suffix *kyac* is applied after a *sup*-ending noun in the sense of "one who desires evil for oneself."
From the word *aśvāghasyāt*, [the form] *āśvam* is derived.
The suffix *śatṛ* is added after that [base].
By the rule *śatrunumaḥ*, the case-ending receives the udātta accent.
*Urūṣya*.
The word *uru* belongs to the *kaṇḍvādi* group; this is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*).
The elision of the accent.
He who brings food even when it is withheld, who awakens the pleasant guest at dawn—the gods bestow him within the house; let the generous giver remain firm in that place.

He who brings food to you, even though he is blameworthy—awaken him as a delightful guest. The divine one kindles [you] in his dwelling; in him let there be lasting wealth, for he is a generous giver. 7.
O Agni, that man who desires food (*agniyate*) and brings to you— offers to give— as food characterized by oblations such as the *puroḍāśa* cake, and who, moreover (*cit*),
bestows the exhilarating Soma, [him you favor].
And he who, honoring the guest as one worthy of hospitality, brings you forth upon his own high altar;

and furthermore, he who, longing for you, the divine one, kindles you within his own home with fuel—upon that man let there be wealth in the form of a son, firm and unshakable through a mind of faith on the Vedic path;
likewise, let him be liberal and endowed with generosity.
*Bharata*:
This is the form of the root *bhṛ* (in the sense of "bearing" and "nourishing") with the addition of the suffix *lyap*.
Its lack of *nighāta* (absence of low pitch) is due to its connection with the word *yat*.
*agniyate*:
one who desires food for oneself;
[the suffix] *kyac*.
The substitution of *i* (itvam) occurs by the rule "kyaci ca.
The short vowel is Vedic (*chāndasa*). [Thus:
*niśiṣat*.
The root *śās* is used in the sense of "instruction.
In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, by the rule *satiśāsasyartibhyaśca*, there is the substitution of *aṭ* for *cl*. By the rule *śāsa idahaloḥ*, there is the substitution of *it* (the vowel *i*).
*udīrat*: from the root *īr* meaning "to move," in the *leṭ* mood, with the substitution of the *parasmaipada* ending.
The augment *aṭ* is added.
Since the augment is unaccented (*anudātta*), the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
By the rule "tiṅi codāttavati" (Pāṇini 8.1.28), there is the suppression of the accent (*nighāta*) of the motion (*gati*).
*indhate*:
[from the root] *indh* in the sense of "to shine" (*dīptau*);
in the present tense (*laṭ*), there is an irregular substitution (*vyatyayena*) for the suffix *śap*.

Because it belongs to the *rudhādi* class, the suffix *śnam* is applied; [by the rule] "the elision of *śna*" (*śnalopaḥ*), [the form is derived]. 1. *na-sivadānaḥ*: *sivadānaḥ*. 2. In the variants *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *pha*, and *bha*, the phrase "'svatavān ... is not stated. 3. In the variants *na*, *la*, and *sa*, the word "'sarvasmāt'" is not present. 4. In the variants *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *pha*, and *bha*, the sequence "'jabharat ... kyac'" is not present. 5. *la*: "Food" (*anna*) characterized by the oblation (*havis*), such as the *puroḍāśa* cake and so forth. 6. In the variants *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *pha*, *bha*, and *sa*, the term "*devatvam*" (divinity) is present. 7. *ta*: "The accent of the verbal root" (*dhātusvaraḥ*). *Ka.* 2.64.

Thus, there is the elision of the *nakāra* (n) of the verbal root (*dhātu*). Because it is not a *kiṅ* suffix, there is no elision of the *as* (the *asun* suffix). Due to its connection with *yadvṛtta*, there is no *anighāta*; rather, it has the accent of the verb (*śramaḥ svaraḥ*). [The word] *dāsvān*: from the root *dās* in the sense of "giving" (*dāne*), the *kvip* suffix is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*) according to the rule for *saṃpad-ādi*. Then, the *matup* suffix is added in the sense of "one who possesses that" (*tadasyāsti*). The substitution of *v* for *m* occurs by the rule *mādupadhāyāḥ*. Since the suffix is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal root remains.
Whoever praises you at evening or at dawn, or who, possessing oblations, makes you his friend— you,
like a horse in its own stable, bringer of golden light, deliver the donor from distress.
Whoever praises you by night or at dawn, or whoever, possessing oblations, makes you dear—him, like a spirited horse in his own stall, bring across from distress, O giver of gifts. 8.
O Agni, that man who praises you at every *doṣā*—

that is, at night— and who praises you at *uṣas*, the time of dawn; or whatever sacrificer, possessing the oblation (*haviṣmān*), having prepared the sacrificial offering, shall make you dear by means of the oblations, pleasing you with them.

Now, you who possess golden trappings like a horse, carry that sacrificer—the donor who has offered the oblation—to the further shore beyond the distress of poverty, as a horse carries one within its own stall;
the meaning is: bestow abundant wealth upon that sacrificer.
The suffixes *doṣ* and *praśaṃsān* take the form *ākāra* after the seventh case.
The term *śaṃyu* is used in the sense of praise (*stuti*). The form *kṛṇavate* is derived from the root with the addition of the augment *āṭ* in the *leṭ* mood.
From the root *kṛv* in the sense of "to injure" or "to do," in the *leṭ* mood, the suffix *up* is applied by the rule *dhinvikṛṇvyoracca*.
The augment *aṭ* is added by the rule *leṭo'ḍāṭau*. Due to its connection with a word beginning with *yat*, there is no *anighāta* (lack of accentuation).
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
[The word] *hemyāvān* [is derived as follows]:
it is worthy of gold (*hema*).

Regarding the form *pīparaḥ*: it is the form of the root *pṛ* (meaning "to protect" and "to fill") in its causative (*pyant*) form, in the *luṅ* tense with the *caṅ* suffix, according to the rule *chandasi ca*.
The elision of the accent (nighāta).

But he who brings gifts to you, O Agni, the immortal, and prepares worship for you with uplifted ladle—he, though laboring, shall not be deprived of wealth; nor shall distress encompass him, for you ward off the malice of the enemy.

O Agni, he who brings service to you, the immortal one, and offers oblations with uplifted ladle—may that man, though striving, not be deprived of wealth; may the day never encompass him for the sake of the malicious.

O Agni, that sacrificer who shall offer oblations (*haviṣ*) to you, the immortal one, free from the law of death—he who, with uplifted ladle and well-prepared ladle, performs service (*duvas*) for you, and being diligent (*śaśamāna*), offers praise—that sacrificer shall not be separated from wealth (*rāyas*); he shall never be deprived of riches. The "day" (*ahas*)—meaning the day of slaughter, the evil—belonging to the malevolent one who desires to harm, shall not encompass (*pari varat*) this sacrificer; it shall not touch him. *dāśat*: from the root *dāś* (to give), in the *leṭ* mood, with the augment *yāṭ*. *tve*: the form of the locative singular; by the rule *supāṃ suluk*, the ending *m* is replaced by *śe*. *kṛṇavate*: because of its connection with a word beginning with *yat* (*yadvṛtta-yoga*), there is no *nighāta* (lack of accent). *yosat*: from the root *yu* (to mix/separate), in the *leṭ* mood; by the rule *sibbahulam*, the suffix *sip* is used, with the augment *aṭ* and *nighāta*. *varat*: from the root *vṛñ* (to choose/encompass), in the *leṭ* mood.
1. Because of the absence of *k*, *kh*, *g*, *c*, *ṇ*, *t*, *n*, *ph*, *bh*, or *s* followed by *kit*; 2. *tatvā* means "you";
3. *phatathā*.

4. Either out of praise for you, or being possessed of the oblation (*haviṣmant*), they make you their beloved. 5. [The variants] *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *pha*, *bha*, and *sa* do not have *tam*; *dha* has *tam*; *la* has *tādṛśam*. 6. [The variants] *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ga*, and *sa* do not have *saṃyatasruk*.

O Agni, you who, as a god, graciously accept the well-prepared sacrifice of the mortal man, may that most youthful Hotṛ-priest be pleased with him; for you are the strengthener of the one who serves you.

O Agni, that mortal whose well-performed sacrifice you, the god, have accepted with favor while bestowing gifts—may that oblation be pleasing to you, O youngest one; may we be the increasers of that worshipper. 10.

O Agni, you who are ungrudging, rejoicing, a god, and shining—may you enjoy (*jujoṣaḥ*), that is, accept, the well-placed, unimpaired food consisting of oblations, intended for you, belonging to whichever mortal man; O youngest one, may that sacrificer, being the Hotṛ priest, be truly pleased.

"May we become the associates of that sacrificer; for that sacrificer who, performing the ritual, leaves no residue, may we—the Hotṛ and the others—be the increasers, the ones who cause his sacrifice to prosper."
*Jujoṣaḥ*: from the root *jupī*, meaning "to love" or "to serve," with the *ślu* affix applied according to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi* (in the Vedic language, [affixes] are used diversely),
and the augment *aṭ*.
The vowel is practiced [as follows]:
*sudhitam*.
In the case of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) of the root *dhā*, the substitution of *dhi* occurs by virtue of the rule "sudhitavasudhita" (Pāṇini 7.4.45).
In the phrase *gatiranantaraḥ*, the accent belongs to *gati*.
[In the word] *asāma*,
there is the augment *āṭ* by the rule *āḍuttamasya picca* applied to the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *as*.
Because the final syllable of *uttama* is *pitta*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*); thus, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains:
*vidhataḥ*.
[The root] *vidha* means "to arrange" or "to ordain."
It belongs to the *tudādi* class;
the case ending is acute by virtue of the rule "śatṛnumaḥ."
O wise one, drive away the alien mind and increase our own thought, as you drive away the sorrows from mortals with your back turned.
O noble god, grant us wealth through your self-dependent power; bestow upon us freedom and protect us from bondage.

Mind, the mindless, the one who possesses thought—may the wise one discern them. Like a chariot-seat, may he drive away both the crooked and the straight among mortals. O noble God, grant us wealth with good protection; bestow upon us freedom and ward off bondage. 11.

The wise one, Agni, who knows the deeds of living beings—whether they be meritorious or sinful—“let him distinguish” (*vicinavat*) “the conscious” (*citta*), which is to be known as merit, from “the unconscious” (*acitta*), which is not to be accepted and is thus non-conscious, being sin. Or alternatively: let him distinguish knowledge (*citta*) from ignorance (*acitta*). In this regard, there is an illustration: “just as a groom (*pāla*) distinguishes on the back (*pṛṣṭha*) the horses’ desirable (*vītā*) and lovely parts from their difficult-to-bear (*vṛjinā*) and undesirable backs, separating them according to what is to be rejected or accepted. Furthermore, let him separate mortals—those who perform meritorious acts from those who do not. O divine Agni, for the sake of wealth (*rāye*) consisting of excellent offspring (*svapṛtyāya*), make us [possessors] of it; and grant us *Diti*, the giver; and protect us from *Aditi* (the non-giver)—here the accusative is used in the sense of the ablative. *Citam*: from the root *citī* (to perceive/know); the suffix *kin* is added in the feminine; due to the *nit* designation, it is udātta-accented on the first syllable. *Vicinvat*: from the root *cinoti*; the *lyap*-augment is applied. *Ditim*: from the root *dāṇ* (to give); the suffix *kin* is added in the sense of the agent. *Rāsva*: from the root *rā* (to give); in the imperative (*loṭ*), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used by irregular substitution. The initial accent is not elided because of the conjunction with *ca* (according to the rule *ca-vā-yoge prathamā*).
1. The reading “ramamāṇaḥ” is absent in manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, and Sa.
2. Manuscripts Kha, Ga, Gha, Ca, Ṇa, Na, Jha, and Bha read “sevase.
3. Manuscripts Dha, La, and Sa [read] “doṣopādeyatvena.”
4. [The suffixes] *ki*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, and *bha* are used after verbal roots ending in *kṛ* when the object is expressed; *kin* is used after roots ending in *l*.
The undeceived poets, maintaining the order in the dwellings of the non-giver, have sung praises to the Sage.
Therefore, O Agni, you who are worthy of being seen, behold these wondrous ones with your feet, according to the ways of the noble one.

The poets have sharpened the poet; the undeceived ones, establishing him in the dwellings of the living man. Therefore, O Agni, you should behold these visible things with your feet—the wondrous work of the noble one through his courses. 12.

O Agni, dwelling in the dwellings—that is, the houses—of the living man, you who are undeceived (unassailable by anyone), acting as sustainers, you wise ones, the seers, have exhorted you, the sage, saying, "Be the Hotṛ-priest.

For this reason, O Lord of the sacrifice, you should behold with your own radiant powers—the feet that are ever-moving—these gods, Indra and the others, who are visible, worthy of being seen, and endowed with wondrous forms.
*dṛśyān* | [The root] *dṛśir* [is used] in the sense of "seeing. [According to] Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.110: *ṛdupadhāccākṛpicṛteḥ*.

O Agni, indeed, we have fashioned you with our feet, with our hands, with our bodies, and with our other limbs; for the sake of accomplishing our work, we have approached you. Therefore, being skillful in action, aspiring after their rites, and pervading them, those Aṅgirases bore you—the Truth, the Reality—within their *bhurijas*.
By *bhurijas* are meant the two arms, which possess the capacity for performing actions and for grasping objects.
By means of their *apás*—the activity known as mantra—they exert themselves; they raise them up.
Therein is an illustration:
like a chariot.
Just as carpenters, craftsmen, or travelers moving along a road lift a chariot with their two hands, so too [is it here];
or rather,
with the two arms (*bhurij*).
The two worlds, heaven and earth, are called *bhurijau* because they support both gods and humans;
between them, by means of their service (*apas*), they sustain—that is, they uphold—the truly existent Agni.
Now, regarding the *saṃhitā*:
in the case of the particle *agha*, as in "naḥ pitaraḥ parāsaḥ pratnāso agne ṛtam āśuṣāṇāḥ."
The singers of hymns, chanting their praises, have uncovered the earth with their pure rays and have released the floods of water.
Now, just as our ancient, far-distant fathers of old, aspiring toward *ṛta* in the beginning, went toward pure vision; those who recited hymns, cleaving the earth, disclosed the ruddy dawns. 16.

O Agni, our ancestors, the Aṅgirases—the most excellent, ancient, and primordial ones—who, aspiring toward and attaining the *ṛta*, the sacrifice that has become truth, according to the proper manner, attained the pure, radiant station;
likewise, they attained spiritual vision and splendor.

Furthermore: "The Aṅgirases—the reciters of hymns (*ukthas*), that is, the chanters of the *śastras*—shattering (*bhindantaḥ*) the darkness or evil that causes destruction (*kṣāma*), uncovered (*avā-vran*) the ruddy-colored (*aruṇīḥ*) cows, which had been carried off by the Paṇis;
that is, they revealed them (the Dawns). This is the meaning.
The root *iṇ* means "to go.
In the *laṅ* (imperfect) tense, the *yaṇ* substitution [of *i* for *y*] applies according to the rule *iṇo yaṇ*.
The augment *aṭ* occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
[The word] *dīdhitim* is derived from the root *dīdhīṅ* in the sense of "shining" or "playing"; the shortening [of the vowel] is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
The word *nintva* is udātta on its first syllable. Regarding *ukthaśāsaḥ*:

when the word *uktha* is used as an upapada, from the root *śaṃs* in the sense of "praising," the suffix *ṇivan* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.2.71 (*mantre śvetavahokthaśaspuroḍāśo ṇivan*), and the elision of the suffixal *nakāra* occurs by means of a specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*).
The short vowel at the end of the word is a Vedic archaism (*chāndasa*).
*Aruṇīḥ* [is formed] with the feminine suffix *ṅīp* from the *gaura*-class.
The single substitute vowel [is formed].
[In the case of] *vran*, there is the substitution of *cli* for the *laṅ* of the root *vṛ* by the rule "in a mantra, [the *cli* of] *ghas* etc. is elided.
The elision of the accent.
For the *āprī* verses of the oblation to Indra, the *yājyā* is "O you of good deeds" (*sukarmāṇaḥ*).
And it is recited: "O all you gods of good deeds, radiant ones, seeking the gods, come hither" (*sukarmāṇaḥ suruco devayanto viśve devāsa ā gata*; Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.9).
Performing good deeds, radiant, seeking the gods, like smiths forging metal, the gods have established their births;
kindling Agni and strengthening Indra, they have come, surrounding themselves with a vast herd of cattle.
Performing good deeds, radiant, seeking the gods, like iron—O gods, fashioning their births, purifying Agni, strengthening Indra, and surrounding the wide stall of cattle, they have come. 17.

"Performing good deeds" (*sukarmāṇaḥ*) means those whose rites, such as sacrifices, are well-established; "of beautiful luster" (*surucaḥ*) means possessing excellent radiance; "seeking the gods" (*devayantaḥ*) means desiring the gods; "the gods" (*devāḥ*) refers to the singers who possess the nature of gods; "purifying their own human birth" (*janima dharmantaḥ*) means making their human birth stainless through actions characterized by sacrifice and the like.
In this regard, there is an illustration: "like iron" (*ayo na*).

Just as smiths work with iron by means of food (fuel), even so the Aṅgirases—kindling the fire, inflaming it with oblations, strengthening Indra with Soma or with praise, and sitting around him—surrounded [him].

(Note: 1. *kha-ca-ṇa-na-pha-bha-la* lack *yajñam*; 2. *kha-ca-ṇa-na-bha-sa* have *ca*; 3. *kha-ca-ṇa-bha* lack *uṣaso vā*; 4. *kha-ca-pha* read *tādṛśam*; *bha-la* read *tādṛśaḥ*; 5. *la* lacks *stutyā vā*).

Sinking down, they reached—that is, they attained—the great, wide expanse rich in cattle and abounding in kine. *Sukarmāṇaḥ*: In this compound, the acute accent (*udātta*) falls on the first syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) by the rule *saumanasā*. *Dhmantaḥ*: From the root *dham* (meaning "to sound" or "to blow"). In the present participle (*śatṛ*), there is the substitution of *dhmā* for *dham* according to the *pādhādi* list. Since the suffix *śap* is *pit*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*); thus, the accent of the *śatṛ* (which is a *lasārvadhātuka* suffix) remains. *Vavṛdhantaḥ*: From the root *vṛdh* (meaning "to grow"). The *parasmaipada* ending occurs by way of metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*). In the *śatṛ* suffix, there is the elision (*blu*) of *śap*. *Gavyam*: Meaning "a collection of cows. The suffix *ya* is applied by the rule *khalagorathāt*. *Agman*: This is the form of the root *gam* in the *luṅ* tense, with the *l* and *luk* elided.
Like herds of cattle, you have driven forth the mortal’s thought; O fierce ones, you are the leaders of the gods’ sacrifice.
Even for mortals, you are the mistress of wide dominion, the one who is never to be led astray, even in the weaving of the lower mortal world.

Like herds of cattle toward a hungry man, he has been drawn toward the birthplace of the gods, O fierce one; even the Urvaśīs yearned for mortals for their increase, and [so did] the noble ones of the lower living world. 18.
O Agni of fierce splendor, you who belong to the Angirases among the gods, this sacrifice which bestows cattle was seen by Indra all around in the vicinity of the mountain;
there is an illustration for this: "like a herd."
Just as people see herds of cattle among the livestock of those possessing food and dwelling in houses filled with provisions,

so it is here— or rather, O Agni, this person who is the attendant of yours, the host of Aṅgirases, who performs the sacrifice for the gods such as Indra and others, sees from nearby the cattle that were carried away by the Paṇis, as if they were being eaten on all sides.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
just as when a bull (*kṣumat*) makes a sound, the herds of cattle see the animals in their respective herds,
so too [do they see] the *urvaśīs*— those who have become wide for mortals, that is, for human beings.

"From the wide [feet] he is heard; by the wide [feet] he prospers," says Yāska (Nirukta 5.13). The subjects were fashioned; by means of those cows that had been brought forth, they became capable and efficient.
Moreover, a noble master who has acquired wealth in cattle is capable of increasing—that is, augmenting—this very wealth that has been sown and poured forth;
likewise, he is capable of providing nourishment for living beings, such as servants and others.
As in *yūthā-iva*.
Or, by the rule for the seventh case, there is the substitution of *ḍā* for *śas*. As in *kṣumati*.
*Kṣut* is a name for food;
or else, [it derives from] the root *dukṣu*, meaning "to sound."

The suffix *kip* is used in the sense of existence (*bhāve*). The elision of the letter *t* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). Then, the suffix *matup* is applied according to the rule "that which belongs to this" (*tadasyāsti*).
The acute accent on *matup* is due to the rule "hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup.
[The verb] *ahyat* [is used] in the sense of "proclaiming" (*prakathane*) according to the root *lyā*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, the substitute *aṅ* is applied by the rule "after the roots *as*, *vac*, and *khyā*, *aṅ* [is substituted for *cli*]. There is elision of the final *ā*. [Thus, the form is] *janima*.
The root *jan* is used in the sense of manifestation.
According to the rule "from *ha* and *jan*, the suffix *imanin*," the suffix *imanin* is applied.
Because it has the marker *ṇi*, it is udātta on the first syllable.
They did not show compassion (*akṛpan*).
[The root] *kṛpū* [is used] in the sense of capability (*sāmarthya*).
In the *laṅ* tense, by the rule "there is frequent elision (*bahulam*) of the suffix (*vikaraṇa*) in the Veda," there is elision of the suffix.
The augment *ruṭ* is applied.
We have become singers for you, O skillful worker; we have approached the shining dawns as the sacred law.
The eye of the god, born from the navel, has been manifested manifoldly as perfect and most radiant.

We have become skillful artisans for you; the radiant dawns have clothed themselves in the Truth (Ṛta). They have brought forth Agni—the perfect, manifold, and most brilliant one—the beautiful eye of the God who knows all things. 19.

1. In the manuscripts kha, ca, ṇa, na, bha, and sa, the phrase "sukarmāṇaḥ ... svaraḥ" is absent. In ta and la, there is the state of being *anudātta*. 2. In the manuscripts kha, ca, ta, bha, and sa, it is the *gaṇa* of the Aṅgirases; in ṇa and na, it is the *gaṇa* of the Aṅgirasas.
O Agni, we have performed—that is, we do—your service (*paricaraṇam*). By that deed, we have become *svapasaḥ*, those of beautiful action.
The radiant Dawns (*vibhātīḥ*), shining forth, clothe themselves in your *ṛtam*, your splendor.
The meaning is that they sustain [him].
Likewise, those Dawns sustain Agni—who is *anna* (food) in its fullness, who shines beautifully (*suśrandam*) in many ways (*purudhā*), or who possesses beautiful gold (*suhiraṇya*)—in various ways.

Furthermore, as we polish (*mamṛjataḥ*) your beautiful, heart-captivating eye—that is, your radiant luster—as you shine like a god, we have become skillful workers (*svapasaḥ*); this is how it connects with the preceding verse.
*akarma*: from the root *kṛ* (to do) in the *laṅ* tense; the suffix is elided by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (in the Vedic language, there is diversely elision). *marmṛjataḥ*.
The root *mṛj* means "to purify.
When the *yaṅ* affix is elided (*yaṅluk*), the augment *rak* is added to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) by the rule "hrig-ṛk-oca-luki.
As for the others, there is an absence of the *num* augment according to the rule "nāvyastāc-chatuḥ."
One who has practiced the musical tones.
O Ordainer, we have uttered these foremost hymns for you, the Seer; may you take pleasure in them.
Shine forth and make us more prosperous; O possessor of many boons, bestow upon us great wealth.
These hymns of praise, O Agni, O Ordainer, we have spoken for you, the Seer; accept them with favor. Blaze forth; make us more prosperous. Bestow upon us great wealth, O possessor of many boons! 20.
O Agni, O Ordainer, O Seer endowed with wisdom, we have recited these hymns, these praises, for you.
Do you take pleasure in them, enjoy them; furthermore, shine forth and blaze up.
Make us, O Puruvara—O you who are praised by many people—most prosperous, exceeding others in wealth. Make it so; bestow upon us great riches. Grant us abundant wealth.
We have said: *avocāma*.
[The root] *vac* is used in the sense of "speaking.
In the *luṅ* tense, the *cli* suffix is replaced by *aṭ*.
The elision of the *n* in *pādādisvāda* [is an example of] *nighāta*.
[In the word] *kṛṇuhi*, this is the form of the root *kṛvi* in the sense of "harming" or "doing," in the imperative mood (*loṭ*).
There is no *nighāta* (absence of accentuation) because it follows a finite verb (*tiṅ*).

Regarding *vasyasaḥ*: after the word *vasu*, when the suffix *īyasun* is added, the suffix *matup* is elided by the rule “*vinmatorluk*” (*Pāṇini* 5.3.65), and once the *ṭi*-portion is elided, the elision of the vowel *ī* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
Regarding *yandhi*: from *yam* with the imperative suffix *loṭ*, there is the elision (*luk*) of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*) by the rule “*bahulaṃ chandasi*” (Pāṇini 2.4.73).

Because the suffix *hi* is optionally treated as having the marker *p* in the Vedic language (*vā chandasi*), the substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs according to the rule “*aditaśca*” (Pāṇini 7.1.46).
The third hymn, consisting of sixteen verses beginning with “ā vo rājānam,” is the seerly composition of Vāmadeva; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and is addressed to Agni.
It is introduced by the words “ā vaḥ pa.ta.śa. Its application (viniyoga) has been stated for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra.
Bring hither for your protection Agni, the king of the sacrifice, the Rudra, the invoker of heaven and earth who sacrifices with truth—
him of golden form, before the unperceived thunderbolt strikes.

Bring hither for your protection the King of the sacrifice, Rudra, the Hotṛ-priest of true worship, Agni who belongs to both heaven and earth—before the unperceived thunderbolt strikes, bring him, the golden-hued one, for our aid.

He— the priests and the sacrificers— [invoke] the King, the sovereign lord of the *adhvara* sacrifice, the Hotṛ-priest who calls upon the gods, Rudra, who roars, who rushes toward his enemies, or who makes his enemies weep; or rather,
[he invokes him] as the very essence of Rudra, for it is said, "This indeed is the body of Agni that is Rudra," [the one] of the two worlds (*rodasyoḥ*).
1. In the manuscripts Kha, Ca, Ṇa, and Na, the word "yajñasya" is absent.

[The seers say: "For your protection from the thunderbolt (*tanayitnu*), you should fashion for yourselves a golden-formed Agni—shining like gold—who dwells between heaven and earth (*dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ*), who is a true-sacrificer (*satyayaja*) and the giver of Satyayajña; or rather, one who worships the gods with a true oblation (*satyena haviṣā*); or rather, one who exists pervading the two worlds (*rodasyoḥ*). From that thunderbolt—which is 'without thought' (*acitta*), meaning death, since death is the withdrawal of all the senses characterized by consciousness—before [that] death occurs, you must fashion him. You should worship Rudra on all sides. Regarding the words: *Rudram*: From the root *rud*, the suffix *rap* is applied according to Uṇādisūtra 2.179 (*roderṇilugvaca*). *Tanayitnoḥ*: The root *tan* means "to sound. It belongs to the *curādi* class. The suffix *istuc* is applied according to Uṇādisūtra 3.309 (*stani-śudhi-pi-gami-man-bhyo ṇeristuc*). It is accented on the final syllable by the *citsvara*. When combined with the case-ending (*sup*), it takes the accent of the single substitute (*ekādeśasvara*). *Kṛṇudhvam*: From the root *kṛvi* in the sense of "injury" or "making. This is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*). [Note: The commentary explains that the *tanayitnu* (thunderbolt) is "without thought" (*acitta*), which refers to death, as death is the cessation of all sensory functions marked by consciousness. One should worship Rudra before such a death arrives.]
This is the proper way: that we, like a longing wife well-adorned for her husband, may sit down facing him, girt about; O skillful one, these [fingers] of mine are turned toward you.

This is the womb. We have fashioned it for you, as a lovingly-desiring, well-dressed wife [prepares] for her husband. Turned hitherward, girt about, sit down; these [fires], O you of skillful workmanship, are turned toward you. 2.

O Agni, we have prepared (*vy-cakṛma*) this place for you, characterized by the *uttaravedi* (high altar). It becomes your station (*sthāna*), O Vayu. Therein is the illustration: like a wife (*jāyā*). Just as a wife, desiring her husband (*uśatī patim*), well-attired (*suvāsāḥ*) in beautiful garments, makes her own place near him, so it is here. O Sva-pāka, Sva-paska—one who knows good deeds—you are *parivītaḥ*, surrounded by the deities to be sacrificed to, or surrounded by splendors. Being *arvācīnaḥ*, turned toward us, sit down (*ni ṣīda*) upon the *uttaravedi*. Of you, standing there, the *vimāḥ*—your flames or praises—proceed *pratīcīḥ*, directed toward you. *Vū*: filler. *Cakṛma*: the form of the root *kṛ* in the perfect tense (*liṭ*). Due to the division of sentences, there is no elision (*jñighāta*). *Arvācīnaḥ*: [the suffix] *svaḥ* is applied according to *vibhāṣājñeradik*. *Parivītaḥ*: from the root *vyeñ* in the sense of "covering" (*saṃvaraṇe*). The past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) is used in the objective sense (*karmaṇi*). Because of its inclusion in the *yajādi* group, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). The accent of the prefix (*gati*) is applied according to *gatiranantaraḥ*.
O wise one, recite a hymn for the immortal god who hears us, the lord of men, the bountiful one worthy of worship; like a presser of Soma, I praise him as the stone that pours forth the sweet juice.

Recite a prayer for him who hears us, for the one worthy of honor, for the one who beholds our thought, for the benevolent one, O Ordainer! Recite a hymn of praise for the immortal god whom I laud, like a pressing-stone, a presser of the sweet juice. 3.

O singer of praises, recite the hymn and the well-recited praise for Agni—the piercer of hymns, the one who hears the singer, the one whose ears are intent upon the song, the one who is vast and ancient, the one who is unwearied and vigilant, the all-seeing watcher of men, the one of beautiful favor and great happiness, the immortal one free from the law of death, the divine one who crosses over. [Recite] the prayer and the hymn;
he is the presser of the exhilarating Soma.

In this regard, there is an illustration: *Note: The text provided contains a mixture of Vedic fragments and commentary. The translation above renders the primary Vedic invocation and its descriptive attributes, followed by the identification of the subject as the Soma-presser.*
"Like the pressing-stone": just as the pressing-stone is the presser of Soma,
so too the sacrificer, performing the pressing of Soma, praises Agni with vigor.
One should recite this for him. 1. [Variants:

kha, gha, ca, ṇa, na, pha, bha, sa—*tanmaraṇāt*. 2. [Variants: kha, ca, na, bha, sa—the word *te* is absent. 3. [Variants: kha, ca, ṇa, pha, bha, sa—*ūtayaḥ*. 4. [Variants: kha, ca, na, bha, la, sa—the phrase *u pūraṇaḥ* is absent. (Ṛgveda 2.65)

[This is] the coordination (*samanvaya*). Or rather: being pressed as the Soma-son of Madhu, [the sacrificer] praises the pressing-stones (*abhimārle*). Therein is an illustration: just as the pressing-stone (*grāvā*), the presser of Soma, makes a sound. For in the verse, "Let them speak forth, let us speak forth to the pressing-stones" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 10.94.1), the agency of making sound is heard for the pressing-stones. Regarding *āśṛṇvate*: by the rule "śaturanumaḥ," the case-ending is acute. Regarding *īḷe*: the root is *īḍ* in the sense of "praising. In the present tense (*laṭ*), there is the elision of *ta* by the rule "lopasta ātmanepadeṣu. Or rather, it is a form derived from the perfect tense (*liṭ*) after the substitution of *eś* for the suffix *ta*.

O Agni, you are manifold; be mindful of this *śamyā* of the sacred law (*ṛta*), for you are well-disposed toward it. When will our hymns be shared in your company? When will our friendships be established in your house?

O Agni, you alone take heed of this our labor for the sake of this *ṛta*, O knower of *ṛta*, you who are well-intentioned. When shall our hymns be shared in the communal feast with you? When will our friendship be established in your house? 4.
O Agni, you alone, through this very rite (*śamyā*)—
the word *śarman* being a name for ritual action—
you become the deity of this rite belonging to us.
O Agni, knower of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), knower of truth, you who are self-possessed, well-performing of rites, and wise—be mindful of the *ṛta*; take notice of our hymn of praise.
When will your shared rejoicings, those chants (*uktha*) and recitations (*śastra*) occasioned by common delight, come to pass?
And when will there be friendships with you in our home?

The words *sadhamādyāni* [are derived as follows]: from the root *mādyati*, which ends in a long vowel (*yantyanta*), the suffix *yat* is applied according to the rule *aco yat*. Then, by the rule *sadha-mādasthayoḥ*, the substitute *sadhā* is applied for the word *saha*.
They exist.
The present tense (*laṭ*) is used here in the sense of the future by the rule "vibhāṣā kadākayoḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.5).
How, O Agni, will you speak to Varuṇa, and how to Dyaus? Where do you proclaim your offense?
How will you speak to Mitra, the bounteous, and to Pṛthivī? What will you say to Aryaman, and where to Bhaga?
How, O Agni, will you speak to Varuṇa? How will you address the Sky? What offense have we committed? How will you speak to Mitra, the bountiful, to the Earth, to Aryaman, and to Bhaga? 5.
O Agni, why do you report that sin of ours to Varuṇa?
For what reason would you announce it preceded by a reproach?
The particle *ha* is used for metrical completion.
To whom—either to the heaven-dwelling world or to the shining Sun—would you report that sin?
What offense (*āgas*) is there against us? That is to say, what sin do we possess? The meaning is: "We have no command to serve you."
Likewise, how would you speak of favor, and how would you declare your offense, toward Mīḷahuṣ, who bestows desired fruits, and toward Mitra and Pṛthivī?
And how, indeed, would you speak to Aryaman the god, and to Bhaga, the deity so named?
*Kathā*:

From the word *kim*, the suffix *thā* is applied by the rule "thā in the sense of cause and in Vedic [usage]" (*thā hetau ca chandasi*). Since it is designated as a case-ending (*vibhakti*) by the rule "those before the pronominal stems beginning with *prāc* are case-endings" (*prāgdiśo vibhaktiḥ*), the substitution of *ka-* for *kim* occurs by the rule "for *kim*, [substitute] *ka-*" (*kimaḥ kaḥ*, Pāṇini 7.2.103).
*mīḷhuṣe*:
[derived from] *miha* "to sprinkle.
*kasu* is a suffix prescribed by the rule "dāśvān sādhuān mīḷvān" (Pāṇini 6.1.12).
The root *brū* means "to speak clearly. In the *leṭ* mood, the augment *aṭ* is applied according to the rule "the augments *aṭ* and *āṭ* [are added] to the *leṭ*."
There is no *nighāta* because it begins with a word-initial syllable (*pādādi*).
Since the augment (*āgama*) is unaccented (*anudātta*), the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) prevails.
1. Kha, ga, ta, na, bha, la, sa: agency. 2. Kha, gha, ca, ṇa, na, pa, pha, bha, sa: what talk can you have of sin? Ta, ta: what talk can you have of that sin?
3. Kha, ca, ṇa, pa, pha, bha: from whom [comes] sin?

What, O Agni, will you say to the one who grows strong in the dwellings of Viṣṇu; what to the wind, the powerful and glorious one; what to the Nāsatyas as they move around the earth; and what to Rudra, the bull, in the mud?

O Agni, what will you say to the gods who dwell in their own abodes when you are growing strong? What will you say to the mighty Vāta, who seeks splendor and moves around the earth? What will you say, O Agni, to the Nāsatyas, the protectors of the dwelling? And what will you say to Rudra, the lord of men? 6.

O Agni, increasing (*vṛdhasānaḥ*)—that is, growing through the offerings of clarified butter (*ghṛta*)—upon the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, such as those of the Āgnīdhra and others, how (*kat*) would you speak? [To whom?

To the one of preeminent strength (*pratavase*), to the one who brings about prosperity (*śubhaṃye*), to the one who moves everywhere (*pariṃjamane*), to the Nāsatya—the leader of truth (*satyasya netre*), or rather, to him for whom no untruth (*asatya*) exists.
"To Vāta, to Vāyu;
or else, according to the recitation of the words, 'to Nāsatya';
[or] 'to the two Nāsatyas, the two Aśvins'."
"Kṣe kṣā"—this refers to the earth (*pṛthivī*).
[It is so called] because living beings (*prāṇinaḥ*) dwell (*kṣiyanti*) or reside (*nivasanty asyām*) upon it. To that earth, "kṣe," how (*katham*) could you speak? (*brūyāḥ*)?
O Agni, O subduer of men, how would you speak—what offense would you utter—to the god Rudra, the slayer of those who commit evil?
*vṛdhasānaḥ*:
[The root] *vṛdh* means "to grow.
Following the recurrence of the suffix *asānac*, the suffix *asānac* is applied by the rule "after the roots *ṛ*, *chid*, *budh*, *madi*, and *sah*, [the suffix *asānac* is] *kit*."
There is *guṇa* substitution because of the *kit* designation.
It is oxytone because of the *cit* designation.
[The form is] *śubhaṃye*.
The root *yā* is used in the sense of "attaining.
[The suffix] *vic* is applied;
furthermore, by the rule "in a *tatpuruṣa* compound, the *kṛt*-suffix is frequently not elided," there is no elision (*aluk*) of the second case ending as well.
*kṛtsvaraḥ* | *kṣe* | *akṣi* [is used] in the senses of "dwelling" and "going."
By the rule "it is seen after other [roots] as well," the suffix *ḍa* is applied in the sense of location (*adhikaraṇa*). From that, the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is added.
In the singular dative case, the elision of the vowel *ā* occurs by means of a formal split (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule "āto dhātoḥ" into "ātaḥ."
*nṛme*:
[derived from] the root *han*, meaning "to injure" or "to go";
the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*.
What [offering] shall we speak to Pūṣan, the lord of abundance, for prosperity; what to Rudra, the well-sacrificing giver of oblations?
What [shall we speak] to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding, regarding seed; what to the great arrow in the abyss?

To whom [do you offer] oblation? To Mahī? To Puṣṭimbharā? To Puṣṇ? What [oblation] to Rudra, the one who accepts good sacrifice? What to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding? What seed, O Agni, do you speak for the sake of the great arrow? 7.

O Agni, why would you speak of evil toward the great one, toward Puṣṭi—the sustainer of nourishment—toward the god named Puṣan? Toward the one worthy of good sacrifice, the performer of excellent rites, or the one who offers oblations; O Agni, you who are the form of the gods and the receiver of oblations, or rather, the giver of oblations by virtue of being the Sviṣṭakṛt.
How could you speak thus to Rudra?
Likewise, how could you speak of "semen"—the cause of decay and sin—to Viṣṇu, who is praised by many (urugāya), or rather, to him of abundant fame;
[how could you speak it] to Śara?
It shatters the ripened plants, thus it is *śaru*; *śaru* is the autumn; or rather, it is the year.
Or else, it is the destructive *nirṛti*.
To the vast, great autumn, or to Nirṛti—how, in what way, would you speak, i.e., utter, evil?
[May there be] nourishment and prosperity.
The root *bhṛ* (in the form *ḍubhṛñ*) means "to support" and "to nourish."
In the word *saṃjñā*, the suffix *khac* is applied by the rule *abhṛtpṛñji* etc.;
the augment *mum* is added to the preceding member by the rule *ahardvipadajantasya mum*;
and because it has the marker *ghit*, it is oxytone (accented on the final syllable).
In a compound, the accent is that of the final member (*kṛtsvara*).
In *haviḥ*, the vowel of the case-ending (*sup*) becomes udātta according to the rule: "And [the vowel] of an anudātta syllable where an udātta is elided."
Regarding *śaru*: the root *śṛ* is used in the sense of "to injure.
The suffix *u* is applied according to the rule beginning with "the suffix *u* is added after *śṛ*, *tviṣ*, *hi*, *trap*, and *as*," etc.
Because of the recurrence of the word "nit," [the suffix] is udātta on its first syllable.

1. After [the letters] kha, gha, ca, ṇa, pa, pha, bha, and ka, [the suffix] pāpa [is applied]. 2. After ta, there is elision (aluk). 3. After kha, ca, ṇa, bha, sa, and gāyamāna, [the suffix] ya is applied. 4. After kha, gha, ca, ṇa, ta, na, bha, sa, and śaru, [the suffix] ya is applied. 5. After kha, ca, ṇa, ta, na, bha, and sa, the augment mum is applied to the preceding word.

How [shall I speak] to the host of the Maruts, to the one who is Truth? How, being questioned, shall I answer back to the great Sun, to Aditi, and to the swift one? O Jātavedas, you who are wise, declare this truly from heaven! 8. How? To the host. Of the Maruts. To the one who is Truth. How? To the Sun. To the great one. Being questioned. Answer back. To Aditi. To the swift one. Truly. From heaven. O Jātavedas. You who are wise. 8.
O Agni, for what reason would you answer my offense to the host of Maruts—that troop which goes according to the cosmic order (*ṛta*) or has become true, and which consists of strength?
Being thus questioned, how would you speak to that great Sun?
Likewise, [how would you speak] to Aditi the divine, and to Vāyu, who moves with swift speed?
To Aditi, or to the undaunted Turas,
how would you answer back my offense? How could you respond to me?
Since this is so, therefore, O *jātavedas* Agni, you who are *cikitvān*— that is, fully cognizant of these [deities]— go toward and accomplish (*sādha*) the shining gods of heaven;
or rather,
accomplish the task of the heavenly world characterized by the carrying of the sacrifice.
In the word *sūre*, because all grammatical rules are optional in the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is the absence of the *yat* suffix for the locative case ending (*ḍeḥ*).
Consequently, by the rule "ato guṇe," the single substitute (pararūpa) is applied.
‘Being questioned’:
[the root] *pṛcch* is used in the sense of ‘desiring to obtain’; the suffix *yak* is applied in the passive (*karman*).
There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by [the rule] *grahy-ādi*. When the *śānac* suffix is unaccented due to being a *lasārvadhātuka*, the accent falls on the *yak* suffix. *Sādha*.
The root *rādh* (in the sense of *sādha*,
"to accomplish" or "to perfect") takes this form by the substitution [of the imperative suffix] for the imperative (*loṭ*) while retaining its causative meaning internally.

By the Truth, I praise the Truth that is firmly established, the raw and the cooked together with the cow, O Agni—sweet and rich in honey. Though she is black, she has swelled with white milk, with this nourishing, glowing fluid. ṛtena | ṛtam | ni'yatam | īḷe | ā | goḥ | āmā | sacā | madhu'mat | pakvam | agne | kṛṣṇā | satī | ruśatā | dhāsinā | eṣā | jārmayeṇa | payasā | pīpāya || 9 ||
O Agni, I implore you for the *ṛta*—the water that is fixed and woven through by the *ṛta*, the sacrifice which has become truth—the milk of the cow, the milch-cow.
The intention is: "I beg of you the milk of the cow for the sake of the *saṃnāyya* and other oblations.
That raw, uncooked cow bears together with herself the cooked milk, which is full of sweetness.

Being black in color, she swells with white milk— the sustainer of living beings— which is generated by the immortal cause for the sake of the *jāmarya*, that is, for the immortality of the *jāḥ* (beings), so called because they are born; with that milk, she causes the progeny to thrive.
It is indeed Your own majesty that You cause this to transform in such a way that You act thus.
*pīpāya* | From the root *pyai*, in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), there is the substitution of *pī* by the rule *liṅyaḍoḥ*.

For by the *ṛta* (Cosmic Order) even the bull has been anointed; Agni, the manly one, with the milk of the back. Moving without wavering, he has gone forth bestowing vigor; the bull Pr̥śni has milked the bright [milk] from her udder. By the *ṛta*, indeed, the bull has been anointed; the manly Agni, with the milk of the back. Without trembling, he has moved, bestowing life-force; the bull Pr̥śni has milked the bright [milk] from her udder.

The Bull (Vṛṣabha), who showers desired fruits, that Man (Pumān), the most excellent, he is Agni. He becomes anointed (akta)—that is, sprinkled—with milk (payas) that is the back (pṛṣṭha), which is the sustainer and has become truth (ṛta).
For "ghi," "m," and "c" are the three fillers (pūraṇāḥ).
The bestower of vitality, the giver of food—that Agni—though remaining motionless, stationed in one place, moves everywhere; he moves by means of his splendor.
Likewise, as a bull that rains down waters, the sun, through the rays, milks the bright path—the atmosphere or the cloud.
He is anointed.
The root *duh* (abjū) is used in the senses of manifestation (*vyakti*), non-momentary duration (*akṣaṇagati*), and milking;
here it is used in the sense of an object (*karman*) with a past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*).
Thus: *duduhe*.
This verbal root takes two objects.
[In the case of] *ūdhas*,
the designation "object" (*karman*) applies by the rule "and that which is not otherwise designated" (*akathitaṃ ca*).
Cleaving the mountain with truth, the Aṅgirases sang together with the cattle;
the heroes obtained the sun’s path for their welfare, and light became manifest when Agni was born.

By means of the *ṛta*, the Aṅgirases split the mountain, cleaving it open; they roared together with the cattle. The heroes sat around for prosperity at the dawning of the dawn; light appeared when Agni was born.

The Aṅgirases, beginning with Medhātithi and others, by means of *ṛta*—that is, by means of sacrifice—as their instrument, splitting and cleaving the mountain (*adri*) that obstructed the cattle, cast it far away.
Then they met together with the cattle.
The leaders (*naraḥ*) of the rites, through their skillful effort (*śunaṃ*), reached around and attained the exertion (*uyama*).
Then the sun also became manifest.
All this occurred when you, O Agni, were produced by friction. Thus it was, O Manu.

O Agni, those immortal ones—the causes of immortality, the immortal rivers unharmed by demons and other such beings, endowed with honeyed waters—those divine rivers, by means of *ṛta* (truth or sacrifice), being true and eternal, flow forth perpetually for the sake of flowing.
In this regard, there is an illustration: like a swift steed.
Just as a road, being urged forward and encouraged at every stage (*sarga*), proceeds onward, so too [do] the waters. [The root] *āp* [is used] in the sense of "pervasion" (*vyāpti*).
‘Āprote: kip hasvaśca’: the suffix *kip* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*), and there is shortening [of the vowel].
By the rule beginning with ‘asṛn’ etc., there is lengthening in the nominative plural (*jas*).
Thus, *prastubhānaḥ*.
The root *stobhati* means "to praise" (*arcati*).

O Yakṣa, may we never be the constant burden of anyone; may we not suffer from a treacherous neighbor or a deceptive kinsman. May we not fall into the debt of one who is ill, nor may we enjoy the wealth of an enemy.
Do not go to the dwelling of any Yakṣa; do not fail the householder, nor the friend, nor the younger brother before his elder. May we, as the righteous, never suffer for the debt of a kinsman. 13.

O Agni, do not ever go—never at any time—to the sacrifice of any person whatsoever who seeks to harm us. Do not go to the sacrifice of a malicious neighbor who intends to injure us; likewise, do not go to the sacrifice of a kinsman other than my own blood-relation.
Likewise, as a younger brother should not desire the sacrificial offering (*havis*) due to his crooked-minded elder brother, as one would not desire the debt of a debtor;
so too may we not enjoy the wealth capable of providing enjoyment belonging to a friend or an enemy.
Rather, may we enjoy only the wealth given by you.
Huraḥ:

O Agni, through these my *arkas*—praiseworthy hymns—be well-disposed, that is, possess a beautiful mind. O Hero, together with our *manmas*, the praises, touch—that is, accept—these *vājas*, our offerings characterized by oblations.
Moreover, O Aṅgiras:
Agni is called Aṅgiras because he moves toward (*aṅgati*) and reaches the oblations (*havīṃṣi*).
Or else:
“The embers that were there became the Aṅgirases” (AiB 3.34); such is the Brāhmaṇa.
Because they are the cause of Agni, the Aṅgirases possess the nature of being his progenitors.
And regarding their causality, there is the mantra: “Those who are the sons of the Aṅgirases, they were born from Agni” (ṚV 10.62.5).
O such Agni, take pleasure in—that is, accept—these *brahmāṇi*, the mantras.
*Devavātā*: having gone to the gods; that is to say, having arrived to praise the gods.
May such praise—this recitation—extol you; may it cause you to grow.
Touch!
[The root *spṛś* means "to touch."]
The *tudādi* group [of roots].
*Devavātā*. [From] the root *vā*, meaning "to go" and "to smell."
In the expression ‘gayarthārthakarmaka’, the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the agent (*kartari*).
The word ‘deva’ ends in the suffix *yac*, belonging to the *pacādyac* class.
In the word *ke ca*, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the word ending in the dative case applies.
O Agni, Ordainer, I have proclaimed with my thoughts all these secret ways,
hidden words, and poetic utterances for you, the wise one— the inspired singer— with hymns of praise.
All these secret ways, O Agni, you who are wise and ordainer—these hidden words, these poetic utterances for the seer—I have proclaimed to you with my thoughts and hymns, as to a sage. 16.

O Agni, you who are the piercer (*vedhas*), the ordainer (*vidhātṛ*), the wise one possessing knowledge of the sphere of ritual action (*karma-viṣaya-jñānavat*), and the seer (*kavi*) of far-reaching vision—to you [I offer] these *nīthāni*: means of attaining results; *niṇyāni*: things to be led out or interpreted; *gūḍhāni*: hidden; *nivacanāni*: things to be spoken most intimately; and *kāvyāni*: poetic compositions made by the wise (*medhāvin*). Accompanied by *matibhiḥ*—thoughts worthy of reflection—*ukthaiḥ* (hymns), and *śastraiḥ* (recitations), I, the inspired singer (*vipra*), the wise one, have praised (*aśaṃsiṣam*) all these words and utterances.
The meaning is: "Accept them."
The fourth hymn, consisting of fifteen verses beginning with “kṛṇuṣva,” is the Ṛṣi Vāmadeva’s composition; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and has the Rakṣohā as its deity.
The Anukramaṇī states: “kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ... is a Rakṣoghna [hymn].
Its application is in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina Śastra.
In the *pravargya* ritual, during the *abhiṣṭava* (recitation), five verses beginning with "kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ" are prescribed for use.
This is stated in the Sūtra: "kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīm—these five" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 4.6).
Spread out your power like a wide net; go forth like a mighty king with this [chariot].
Rending along your own path, you are an archer; pierce the Rakṣas with your burning heats.

Display your power like a wide-spreading net; go forth like a fierce king with this [weapon], rending asunder that net of yours. You are an archer; pierce the *rakṣas*! Burn it with your burning heat! 1.
O Agni, create, that is, perform and extend, your mass of splendor. In this regard, there is an illustration: "like a snare."

Just as a hunter spreads a wide net—*prasiti* being so called because it is *prakarṣeṇa sīyate*, meaning it is extensively bound or spread—such a net for the purpose of catching birds [is used]. (Note: Regarding the variant readings, *madanīyaiḥ*, *bhavadīyaiḥ*, and *mahanīyaiḥ* are offered.)
2. In the versions *kha*, *ca*, *na*, *la*, and *sa*, the word ‘agnāni’ does not exist.

3. In *kha*, *ca*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*, it is ‘tatkāraṇam’; in *na* and *bha*, it is ‘tatkāraṇe’. 4. In *kha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *na*, *pha*, *bha*, and *sa*, it is for the purpose of [the word] ‘devatī’ (or ‘devatā’).
5. The letters kha, gha, ca, ṇa, pa, pha, and ma are the conveyors [of the mantra]. 6. Ru, ca, ṇa, and bha—these are the universal [syllables].
Just as one spreads [a net] through dense forests, so too you should deploy a great force before you in order to slay the rākṣasas.
Endowed with an army of elephants that are fearless and possessed of fiery vigor, you should go; depart to slay the demons.
In this regard, there is an illustration: like a king.
Just as one who possesses *amā* (proximity) is called *ama*,
so too one who conducts himself together with the king is an *amātya* (minister).
One who possesses that;
or alternatively, *ama* is sickness, meaning disease.
He possesses the diseases that are to be inflicted upon his enemies;
the meaning is that he is like a disease unto his enemies.
Just as a king, being joined with an *ibha*—that is, an elephant—advances against the enemy force, so too is he.
Furthermore, *tṛptīm*.
*Tṛpti* is a name for "swift. Following *prasitim*, meaning an excellent army, *anūtṛṇānaḥ*, meaning pursuing or following after it.
Alternatively:
the word *tṛptīm* is used in the accusative case with the sense of the instrumental;
[thus it means] "with a swift, gliding, continuous, and uninterrupted movement. *Dūṇānaḥ* means "destroying," i.e., harming the enemy army. *Astā* means "a hurler," i.e., one who casts down enemies.
O most powerful one, with your most excellent splendors, pierce and strike down the *rākṣasas*, the demons.
Regarding this, the *Nirukta* states: "Perform your *pāja*;
*pāja* is so called because of protecting (*pālana*)."
Like the earth as a stretch;
"prasita" means either from the act of overpowering, or a net.
Go like a king accompanied by ministers, with followers, and with his own troops—or like one with the elephant Airāvata, that fearless beast.
"By satisfaction, through abundance, being difficult to overcome;

'tṛpti' is a name for speed, from the root *tṛ* (to cross over) or *tvar* (to hasten). You are a hurler, O dispeller of demons, most burning with heat; 'most burning' means with the most scorching [heat]" (Nirukta 6.12).
*Kṛṇuṣva*. [The root] *kṛv* is used in the senses of "injuring" and "doing. In the imperative (*loṭ*), the suffix *up* is applied according to the rule *dhinvikṛṇvyora ca*.
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).

As for the accent of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*), although it is "later taught" (*satiśiṣṭa*), it does not override the accent of the verbal root (*dhātu-svara*) which is "earlier taught" (*lambādi*); thus, there is the accent of the verbal root (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.198).
All thy labors fly swiftly; touch them with boldness as thou blazest forth.
O Agni, with thy tongue cast forth thy glowing heats like winged insects; unbound, scatter thy firebrands in every direction.

O Agni, with your swift-moving flames you fly; touch them all boldly as you blaze forth. With your tongue, cast out your heats like winged birds; unrestrained, let loose your firebrands in every direction.
O Agni, your toiling rays, wearying yet swift-moving, fall and spread forth on all sides.
Blazing intensely, you, with your bold and overpowering mass of brilliance, burn the enemies away in succession.
[The poet] now shows the means of burning them:

Unbound by others and unrestrained, you— by means of the *juhū* (the sacrificial ladle, so called because oblations are poured into it), which is the flame of the fire— scatter and spread forth in every direction with the threefold *tapaḥ* (torments,
i.e., heat-radiations), *pataṅkān* (falling sparks), and *ulkāḥ* (meteors).
*Āśuyā*:
from the word *āśu*, the suffix *yāc* is applied by the rule *supāṃ suluk* (*Pāṇini 7.1.39*),
and it bears the *cit-svara* accent.
*Dhṛṣatā*: from the root *dhṛṣ* in the sense of "to overpower," belonging to the curādigaṇa (class 10);
the suffix *śa* is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
In *śataranumaḥ*, the vowel of the case-ending is udātta.
In *juhvā*, the suffix *kip* is applied by the rule *juhoter dīrghaś ca*; there is reduplication and lengthening of the vowel.

Regarding the word *asaṃditaḥ*: by the rule *“udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt”* (Pāṇini 6.1.174), the case-ending would have been udātta; however, this is prohibited by the rule *“no’dhāvaḥ”* (Pāṇini 6.1.175). Consequently, by the rule *“udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ”* (Pāṇini 8.2.4), the resulting *yaṇ* vowel becomes svarita. [The root] *dru* [is used] in the sense of “breaking apart.”
The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used in the sense of the object (*karman*). In the form *catitvā*, there is the substitution of *it*.
In a compound with the negative particle *nañ*, it bears the accent of that [particle].

1. *kha-ga-ca-ṇa-ma-rājā* | 2. *kha-ga-ca-ṇa-bha-anuvṛddhayā* | 3. *kha-ga-ca-ṇa-sa-taptamaiḥ* | 4. *na-la-ma-‘tṛptamaiḥ* (the mark *^* does not exist) | 5. *kha-ga-ca-ta-na-bha-la-sa-dhṛṣa* | 6. *kha-ga-ca-ṇa-bha-napsamāse* | O most swift one, send forth your spies; be an undeceivable protector of this people.
O Agni, let no one who plots evil against us from afar or nearby prevail over you with his assault.

Touch [them]! Release [them]! Be the swiftest protector of this people, you who are undeceivable. O Agni, let no one who utters evil against us—whether he be far away or near—dare to cause you any distress. 3.

O Agni, you who are the swiftest—most rapid—release your spies, those rays or scouts that drive away adversaries, for the sake of discerning truth from falsehood; specifically, direct them against the enemies.
Being undeceived, unhurt by anyone, become the protector (*pāyu*) of this people (*viś*), our progeny and the like.
To the question of why such protection is required, he says:
O Protector, from that enemy who is far from us— an *aghaśaṃsa*, one whose speech, intention, or proclamation is evil (*agha*)—
and from that enemy who stands near us, protect us from both such types of foes.
Furthermore, let no one whatsoever—no tormentor or obstructing Rākṣasa belonging to you—dare to harm us;
that is to say, let no one cause us any insult or injury.
*anti*: there is elision of the *ka* and following sounds of *antikasya*, and it is acute-accented (*āśudātta*). *agne*.
Because it begins with *pāda*, it has the udātta accent on the first syllable (*pādikam*).
In the *saṃhitā* reading of *mārkiṣṭe*, the change to *ṣ* occurs according to the rule *yuṣmattattakṣuḥ-antaḥ-pādam*.
[The form] is *dadharṣīt*.
The root *dhṛp* means "to overcome.
In the *laṅ* [tense], by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is *ślu*-elision of the *śap* [suffix].
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the addition of the augment *īṭ* to the *tip* [suffix].
The elision of the accent.
Arise, O Agni! Spread yourself out; burn down our enemies with your heat. O kindled one, whoever has directed hostility toward us, consume him like dry wood, casting him low.

Arise, O Agni! Stand forth and spread yourself out; burn down our enemies with your sharp-pointed weapon. O Kindled One, whoever has directed hostility toward us, consume him downward like dry brushwood. 4.

O you of sharp weapons! He whose weapons—meaning flames—are sharp and piercing; such you, O Agni, arise, be prepared for the slaying of the Rākṣasas. Spread yourself out against the enemies; extend your mass of flames. With those masses of brilliance, utterly burn (ni oṣatāt) the adversaries, the enemies. O Samidhāna, O Agni who are kindled and shining, that man who has practiced *arāti* toward us—this is a reference to the state of being; he who acts with hostility (*arātitva*) or enmity, or who offers gifts to the enemy—that man you must burn down, consume, making him low-lying. Here is an illustration: like dry wood. Just as you burn dry, sapless *atas* wood, so [burn him]. Regarding *oṣatāt*: from the root *upa-dāha* (to burn). In the imperative (*loṭ*), by the rule *tubhyoḥ*, there is the substitution of *tāt*. Regarding *dhakṣi*: from the root *daha* in the imperative, by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix. By the rule *ho ḍhaḥ*, there is the change to *ḍha*. Then the *bha*-state occurs. By the rule *paṭhoḥ kaḥ si*, there is the change to *ka*. There is the *nighāta* accent.

1. Those ending in *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*. 2. In *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *sa*—the word ‘*avā*’ does not exist. 3. In *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*: *tīkṣṇajvāla*; *sa-tīvrāḥ*. Ṛgveda 2.66.522; Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 4, Varga 24.

Stand upright; pierce [them] back from us; make manifest thy divine powers, O Agni. Slacken the firm [bonds] of those impelled by the sorcerers; crush the enemies, whether kin or stranger. 5. Or alternatively: [the verse continues as follows].
Slay those enemies who have previously struck a kinsman, and those who have not previously struck a non-kinsman— slay such foes.
Do not remain indifferent, thinking, "This one has been struck."
In the word *āviṣkṛṇuṣva*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs according to the rule *iḍudupadhasya cāpratyayasya* in the *saṃhitā*. In *tanuhi*,
the absence of the elision of *hi* occurs because of the rule *utaśca pratyayācchandasi vāvacanam* applied to the root *tan* in the imperative (*loṭ*).
*yātujūnām*:
[The root] *ju* means "to go";
[the suffix] *kvip* is applied by the rule beginning with *ṛtvi*.
The word *dīrghaḥ* [is used]; the augment *num* after *āmi* is a Vedic usage;
[the form] *mṛṇīhi*.

O youngest one, O most youthful one, or rather, O Agni, you who are the best mixer of the oblations for the gods—whatever man offers *gātu* (praise), which is so called because it is sung (*gīyate*) and uttered, as a *brahman* (a strengthening prayer) that serves as a cause for auspicious arrival, unto you, the sovereign one, who are possessed of movement (*īvate*). (Note: *Gātu* here refers to a hymn of praise, derived from the root *gai*, "to sing," meaning that which is chanted or recited.)
He impels it;
that person knows—meaning he obtains—your auspicious and benevolent wisdom (*sumati*).

For this sacrificer who has performed the hymn of praise, for his sake, O Lord of sacrifices (*arya*), you who are the master of rites, shine forth preeminently (*vi dyaut*) toward all beautiful days (*sudināni*), riches (*rāyaḥ*), resplendent glories (*yumnāni*), and dwellings (*duraḥ*).
Some here accept a division of the sentence:
for the sacrificer who has performed the hymn of praise, all auspicious days— days that bring about prosperity— and riches [come to pass].
They yield milk and other products, thus "rāyaḥ" refers to cattle-wealth; furthermore, "yumnāni," meaning shining objects such as gold and the like, belong to him.
[He is] noble (aryaḥ).
He who performs the rites, that sacrificer, [goes] toward his dwellings, the doors.

1. The syllables *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, and ‘*ca*’ are not present. 2. *na*, *la*, *sa*, *jāmi*, *amajāmim*, *bandhum*, *abandhum*. 3. *kha*, *ga*: *tādṛśān*; *na*, *la*, *sa*: ‘*etādṛśān*’ is not present. 4. *na*, *bha*, *la*, *sa*: *ityapekṣām*. 5. *ṇa*, *la*: *kindhīdhaiṃ*. 6. *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, *sa*: *kalyāṇahetubhūtagamanāya*. 7. *na*, *la*, *sa*: ‘*sarvāṇi*’ is not present. 8. *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *bha*: ‘*śobhanāni dināni*’ is not present. 9. *ca*, *la*: *dhanāni*. 10. *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *sa*: ‘*saḥ*’ is not present.

*vi dyaut*: It shines forth especially. [The root] *ī* means "to go"; [from this] *kip* [is added]. Then, by the rule "*tadasyāsti*" (Pāṇini 5.2.94), the suffix *matup* is added. By the rule "*chandasīraḥ*" (Pāṇini 8.2.15), the *m* of *matup* becomes *v*, resulting in *īran*. [The root] *īr* means "to go. Because it is connected with a word beginning with *yat*, there is no *nighāta* (elision of accent). *Arthaḥ*: [The root] *ṛ* means "to go. The form *arthaḥ*—meaning "master" or "vaiśya"—is derived as a nipātana (irregular formation) ending in the suffix *yat*. As a master (*svāmin*), it has an udātta accent on the final syllable. *Dyaut*: [The root] *dyut* means "to shine. In the Vedic *luṅ* tense, by the rule "*dyudbhyo luṅi*" (Pāṇini 1.3.91), the *parasmaipada* (active voice) is used. By the rule "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" (Pāṇini 6.4.75), there is an absence of the augment *aṭ*.

May there be satisfaction for him who is fortunate and bounteous, who desires to gratify you with constant oblation and hymns throughout his own life in his home; for him, every joyous sacrifice shall be successful.
